bull_bear.body:
- **Rs 5,000 cr equity raise** approved & pending only government nod — a **dilution watch-item** even though CET1 15.56% is comfortable.
- **Provision buffers:** COVID/restructured buffer ~Rs 1,050 cr (≈100% of restructured book, "not really required"), ECL Rs 255 cr already set aside — write-back optionality over coming quarters.
- Growth funded by deposits + refinance, not borrowings ("we are not borrowing and funding").
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Deposit disintermediation** — management flagged an "irreversible" shift of household savings to SIP/MF/demat (even Tier 2-3), pressuring the core deposit franchise → forces reliance on refinance/CDs/equity.
- **NIM compression** — NII (14.5%) lagging advances (27%); further MCLR resets pending; NIM defence hinges on repo-book re-pricing and no more rate cuts.
- **Maharashtra farm debt-waiver:** eligible book Rs 3,500 cr; govt receivable Rs 2,750 cr; farmer share Rs 260 cr; **max haircut Rs 450-500 cr, but Rs 1,700 cr provision already held + Rs 1,100 cr technical write-off** → net positive to OP via TWO recovery; expected within FY27.
- **Cost of deposits +5 bps QoQ** — CASA converting to TD; question is whether it has bottomed.
- **CD ratio elevated** (global 87-88%) — mitigated by refinance framing (81.99%).
- Segment GNPA up QoQ in retail (housing/vehicle/education) and MSME (small ticket), and one Rs 87 cr government account in SMA-2 (called transient); overall stress still improved (−140 bps YoY to 3.18%).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, numbers-fluent, disciplined. Repeated "profitable growth, no compromise on asset quality" as the operating mantra; built a branch-level profitability dashboard and is weighting appraisals on profitable growth. Candid on structural deposit-shift and on choosing 18% guidance conservatively. Highlighted governance/ownership traction: FII holding 0.39% → 6.08% and DII 0.24% → 7.42% (ex-LIC) over 2 years.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Over-delivery with a conservative guide is deliberate** — management treats guidance as "sacrosanct" and prefers to beat than chase; 18% held despite 27% actuals.
- **Refinance is the margin lever**, not bulk deposits — 6-6.5% blended, no CRR/SLR, keeps NIM defended while funding 27% loan growth without CDs.
- **Debt-waiver is a net positive, not a hit** — haircut fully pre-provided; TWO recoveries and Rs 50,000/farmer state incentive add SB balances.
- **New-branch "zero-base" effect** structurally inflates growth vs peers — each of ~200 new branches/yr adds incremental business off a zero base.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital position is comfortable and internally generated: CRAR of 18.64% with CET-1 at 15.56% and Tier I at 16.35%, well above the Mar'26 trough of 15.41% Tier I.
- Capital mix is shifting toward core equity — Tier II has been steadily run down from 4.13% in Sept'24 to 2.29% in Jun'26 while Tier I has risen.
- Equity base has been held constant at 769 crore shares across all five quarters shown, so book value per share growth to Rs 42.62 comes from retained earnings rather than dilution.
- Growth is being part-funded by wholesale borrowings, which rose from Rs 23,730 crore to Rs 38,749 crore over the year as credit growth outpaced deposit growth (global C/D ratio up to 88.82%).
- Risk-weighted assets grew to Rs 2,17,396 crore, dominated by credit risk RWA of Rs 1,90,579 crore, with operational risk RWA stepped up to Rs 25,499 crore.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **RAM:Corporate 63:37.** Retail +25%, Agri +30%, MSME +23%, Corporate +30% (corporate accelerated from ~17-18% run-rate).
- **GIFT-City IBU:** book Rs 8,200 cr in ~8-9 months, $965 mn sanctions, ~2-3% of advances; lower NIM than domestic but sticky corporate relationships + ECB cross-sell. Global yield 8.57% vs domestic 8.66% (13 bps drag).
- **Retail underwriting discipline:** no sanctions below CIBIL 681 (subprime cut-off) in 15 months; ~80% of new home-loan sanctions in prime/super-prime (750+).
- **Treasury:** Rs 266 cr Q1 income incl one-time SR Rs 104 cr; upgraded talent hired from other PSBs.

business.body:
- Public sector bank with Government of India holding 73.60% of equity as on 30th June 2026, with the balance spread across banks/FIs/insurers (7.32%), mutual funds (6.95%), FIIs/NRIs (6.08%) and individuals (5.61%).
- Positions itself as a RAM-led lender: retail, agriculture and MSME together form 62.89% of domestic advances, with corporate and others at 36% and overseas only 3% of global advances.
- Credit standing is presented via external ratings: AA+ (Stable) long-term on Tier II bonds from ICRA/CARE/Infomerics/Acuite/Brickwork, CRISIL A1+ short term, and S&P Global BBB- (Stable) international rating.
- Deck leans on external validation as a mid-sized PSB, citing 'Best Mid-Sized Bank' at the Business Today Banking & Economy Summit 2026, 'Public Sector Bank of the Year' at the FE Best Banks Awards, and IBA/SKOCH/IBEX technology awards.
- Loan-book concentration is skewed to infrastructure (17.73%), housing (16.99%) and agriculture & allied (13.65%), which together cover over 48% of total funded exposure.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Rating migration] The externally rated book above Rs 25 crore has improved in quality mix, with AAA exposure rising to 14% of outstandings from 5% a year earlier, though BB & below also rose to 6% from 2%.
- [Concentration risk] Agriculture carries a structurally elevated sector NPA ratio of 7.58% versus 0.34% in retail and 0.04% in corporate, making it the dominant source of the bank's stressed assets.
- [Macro backdrop] The deck frames the environment via RBI's 6.6% FY27 real GDP growth projection, a repo rate held at 5.25% with neutral stance, and CPI forecast at 5.1%, while flagging geopolitical tension, crude volatility, a weakening rupee and El Nino monsoon risk.
- [Restructured book run-off] Restructured standard advances continue to shrink, from Rs 2,282 crore in Jun'25 to Rs 2,001 crore in Jun'26, led by retail and MSME reduction.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- NIM 3.85% (−10 bps YoY): yield on advances fell 71 bps QoQ as MCLR book (44%) resets to prior FY26 rate cuts; **repo-linked book now 53%** → immediate upside if RBI hikes. MCLR base lifted in last two ALCOs → reset tailwind over next year.
- Cost of deposits 4.38% (−22 bps YoY, **+5 bps QoQ** as CASA converts to retail TD; TD growing 16% vs total 13%).
- **Funding strategy:** avoids high-cost bulk deposits; ~Rs 19,000 cr refinance at blended 6-6.5% (no CRR/SLR loading) → CD ratio 87-88% global / 86% domestic / **81.99% including refinance**.
- Opex +8-9% vs 20%+ balance-sheet growth; staff 17,500 (from ~13,000 two years ago); cost-to-income target <40% (running 36-38%).
- Tax rate: OP-basis 12-13%, PBT-basis 16-17% (rural-advance + bad-debt write-off + DTA benefits).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:

deepdive.thesis: A steady, guidance-beating quarter from a fast-growing mid-cap PSU: business +19% and advances +27% YoY (both above guidance), asset quality held at March levels (GNPA 1.45%, NNPA 0.13%, PCR 98.55%) and profitability strong (OP +21%, PAT +27%, ROA 1.9%, ROE 24.65%). NIM slipped 10 bps to 3.85% on MCLR-reset drag but still 10 bps above the 3.75% guide. Management **explicitly refused to raise the 18% loan-growth guidance** despite over-delivering, is funding growth with refinance/CASA rather than costly bulk deposits, and holds a **Board-approved Rs 5,000 cr equity raise** in reserve for the fast credit growth.
